strings.name: Magnus Carlsen
strings.role: Chess grandmaster · Former classical world champion
strings.summary: Magnus Carlsen is a Norwegian chess grandmaster who joined the world elite as a teenager. He defeated Viswanathan Anand to become classical world champion in 2013, defended the title four times and reached a peak rating of 2882. In 2022 he decided against another classical title defence, while continuing in rapid, blitz and other events, winning his first World Cup in 2023. His sustained results and online presence have broadened chess’s public reach.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verified milestones through 2026-11-10; sources checked on 13 November 2026. This is not an event-by-event or live record.
strings.influence.rationale: His world championship achievements and sustained high ratings have helped drive chess’s development online and its wider public reach.

strings.highlights.classical.title: Classical world championship reign
strings.highlights.classical.text: He won in 2013 and defended in 2014, 2016, 2018 and 2021, then chose not to contest the next title match.
strings.highlights.peak.title: Record peak rating
strings.highlights.peak.text: He first reached a FIDE classical rating of 2882 in 2014, setting the historical record.
strings.timeline.pilot26.title: Won the pilot’s opening blitz
strings.timeline.pilot26.text: He went unbeaten with 7/9 in the opening blitz of the Total Chess pilot in Budapest; this was not the overall event title.
strings.timeline.shared24.title: Shared world blitz title
strings.timeline.shared24.text: After the final tiebreaks, he and Ian Nepomniachtchi shared the 2024 World Blitz Championship Open title.
strings.timeline.cup23.title: First World Cup victory
strings.timeline.cup23.text: He beat R Praggnanandhaa in rapid tiebreaks to win his first FIDE World Cup, a separate event from the world championship match.
strings.timeline.withdraw22.title: Declined another classical defence
strings.timeline.withdraw22.text: He announced that he would not play the next classical world championship match, ending plans for another defence while continuing in other events.
strings.timeline.defence21.title: Fourth successful defence
strings.timeline.defence21.text: He defeated Ian Nepomniachtchi in Dubai to retain the classical world title for the fourth time.
strings.timeline.peak14.title: Reached 2882
strings.timeline.peak14.text: He first reached 2882 on FIDE’s May classical rating list, setting a new historical peak.
strings.timeline.title13.title: Became classical world champion
strings.timeline.title13.text: After winning the Candidates Tournament, he defeated Viswanathan Anand in Chennai to claim his first classical world title.
strings.timeline.gm04.title: Grandmaster at thirteen
strings.timeline.gm04.text: He earned the grandmaster title at 13, already making his mark in international competition as a teenager.
strings.timeline.learn95.title: Introduced to chess
strings.timeline.learn95.text: His father introduced him to chess at about five; training and competition later revealed his talent.
